tables: Phomopsis fungicide sprays are no longer necessary.

In some years and on some varieties, powdery mildew may cause defoliation after harvest. Premature defoliation, especially in early harvested varieties or winter-tender V. vinifera, predisposes the vines to winter injury and reduces bud survival the following spring. Good control of powdery mildew through August greatly reduces disease pressure during the early portion of the following year.
Black rot fungicide sprays are no longer necessary.
